The Story

From North Philly
to the World.

Mike Terrell was born in the Mt. Airy section of Philadelphia and raised in North Philly — a city that shaped his voice, his hunger, and his soul. He started singing in church, joined local gospel groups, and fell in love not just with the music but with the rehearsals, the creativity, the road, and the late-night diners after gigs.

"I knew I wanted to sing after I joined a local church singing group in Philly. The rehearsals, the creative part, the traveling, the late night diners after gigs — I knew this was something I began to fall in love with."

He trained with the Keystone State Boychoir — one of the world's most prestigious youth choral programs, having sung for presidents, popes, and Nobel Peace Prize winners on all seven continents. It was with the KSB that Mike first toured Norway as a young boy. Decades later, Norway would become his #1 streaming city worldwide.

He attended Philadelphia's CAPA — the same legendary institution that produced Boyz II Men, Questlove, Black Thought, and Leslie Odom Jr. — as a Theater major. He then earned a scholarship to Columbia College Chicago, majoring in Music Business Management, before leaving his junior year to play Sammy Davis Jr. as an Equity lead at the Black Ensemble Theater. The Chicago Sun-Times covered it. Playbill covered it.

The move to Los Angeles came during COVID — when his lease expired in Chicago, Terrell chose to trust God and drive west on a TV residual check rather than renew. His first LA gig was a gospel live recording where he connected with elite singers. Isaiah Jaay — a well-known LA singer, social media personality, and grandson of gospel legend Joe Ligon of the Mighty Clouds of Joy — saw Mike's videos on Instagram and referred him to an audition. Out of 100 people in that room, Mike Terrell was one of two selected.

His mother — his superwoman and his rock — sang background vocals for gospel artists in her younger years. Mike is living one of her first loves. Full circle.
